result:
I built B03. Typecheck, the full test suite (42 files, 382 tests), `check:tokens` and the build all pass. I couldn't run the checks inside the pinned container because its image isn't built here, so they ran directly in this environment. The working directory isn't a git repo either, so I couldn't produce a diff. The change touches 6 files in `src/` (well under 800 lines), plus 2 new test files and a journal note.

**What changed**
- **`src/content/drivers.ts`** (new): the six-driver `ROSTER` with the exact names, numbers, body and stripe colours from the spec. `raceDrivers(n)` returns the player followed by the first n−1 AI drivers, and throws if n isn't between 1 and 6.
- **`src/game.ts`**: the hard-coded `LIVERIES` is gone. The scene liveries, car count, minimap colours and driver labels now all come from `raceDrivers(2)`, so the bot is KOSKI #7. The car builder is unchanged.
- **`src/ui/types.ts`**: a new `DriverLabel` type (name and number).
- **`src/ui/race-ui.ts`**: `reset` takes an optional fourth argument, the driver labels. When the race finishes, it sorts the cars by race position and passes the labels on to the finish panel.
- **`src/ui/finish-panel.ts` and `screens.css`**: an ordered list of "NAME · #n" rows. Each row uses the existing caps label style, cream text on the navy card, with no inline styles. The list is hidden when there are no labels.

**Tests**
| AC | Test |
|---|---|
| AC1 | `tests/content/drivers.test.ts`: exact roster values and order, every entry passes `validateLivery` |
| AC2 | same file: one player, no red AI car, AI bodies distinct and equal to `tokens.cars.ai` |
| AC3 | same file: each car uses exactly its body, stripe, cabin and ink colours; roundel is cream and ink; only YOU has the ▼ marker |
| AC4 | same file: BRUNO's cabin faces are all teal with no navy; every other cabin is navy |
| AC5 | same file: `raceDrivers(2)` is YOU #1 then KOSKI #7; `game.ts` imports it and has no livery literal left |
| AC6 | `tests/ui/finish-drivers.test.ts`: with the player 2nd and KOSKI 1st, the panel reads "KOSKI · #7" before "YOU · #1", and the order flips when the player wins |
| AC7 | same file: the three-argument `reset` shows time and best lap with no list; list rows use the label class with no inline style |

All of these fail on `main`. The roster file doesn't exist there, and the finish panel has no driver list.

**Left out on purpose:** UI_RULES doesn't say how a results row should look (panel, chip or plain text), whether YOU's row should be highlighted, or whether the rows should "deal in" with the 40ms stagger it describes. I wrote these up in `journal/runs/2026-11-02/design-request.md` instead of guessing.
